It is! And it is also a design tool. You can use it to create "viral" effects in your designs, products, and campaigns. - How did one small link jumping across "vast distances" seemingly compress the network into a "Small World"? - How might we use this idea in Art/Design? - Try a very tenuous-looking, unlikely *location* to access a new community of users / artists / designers / collaborators? - *Put yourself / your enterprise in *dangerous* postions? ### Moat Building in Business ### Metcalfe's Law ### First Mover Advantage ### ### Discussion Questions - So how does one *scotch/stop* a rumour? Can you [**be vaccinated** against rumours](https://www.complexity-explorables.org/explorables/epidemonic/)? Is there a game-theoretic cost for the vaccination? - How does one be *individual and different* and still *one of the gang*? Is it possible [to be inside and outside the group]{.black .bg-washed-red} at the same time? Is it a good idea [to be an insider and an outsider at the same time?](https://www.beyondintractability.org/essay/insider-partial) - How do [Echo Chambers](https://www.complexity-explorables.org/explorables/echo-chambers/) work? - How does one think of products and ads, or policy messages? (Remember the ["Bell Bajaao" campaign?](https://youtu.be/zmNz0cTcxFU) - There are popular and well-known phrases and ***memes*** in every language! Use them!! - Here is one for you: "Less Than Three!" ## Conclusions - Individual Actions Matter. Because they can be "reverse infections" **and** be contagious, in a positive way. - Correlations between Individual Actions can create "standing waves" or "echoes" on the fabric of society. - Whatsapp "echo chambers" - Popularity of Memes, Songs, and Movie lines - Taglines from Ads, and Products ( e.g. "Think Different". Bah.) ## References 1. The Network Effects Bible. 1. Mitchell Resnick. *Beyond the Centralized Mindset*. 1. Thomas W. Valente.(2012). *Network Interventions*. Science(337) 49. Available here . The term “network interventions” describes the process of using social network data to accelerate behavior change or improve organizational performance. In this Review, four strategies for network interventions are described, each of which has multiple tactical alternatives. 1. Nicholas Christakis. (May 3, 2024). To exploit social contagion, tools are needed to efficiently identify individuals who are better able to initiate cascades. To be maximally useful, such tools should be deployable without having to actually map face-to-face social network interactions. .
